author: TeIq
content:
## Source
.design/m5/44-mobile-app.md — full design.

## What this epic delivers
A constrained mobile client for P1 incident response: receive push, view case read-only, take/release ownership, call senior reviewer. Full moderation workflows stay desktop-only. Explicit non-goal: "moderation from a phone."

## Sub-issues (8 PRs + 1 Q-resolution)
- Q-resolution: confirm platform (Q1), push infra (Q2), external HW keys (Q3), on-call source (Q4), ownership broadcast (Q5)
- PR 1: 1-week prototype spike (Tauri Mobile vs PWA) — measures iOS push latency, Android build path, decides on evidence
- PR 2: backend push subsystem — APNs + FCM in `notifications/push.rs`, `mobile_devices` table, `/api/devices/register` endpoint
- PR 3: mobile app shell + OIDC + ATProto OAuth via OS browser + deep-link callback
- PR 4: read-only case view subset reusing v1 `PolarisApiClient`
- PR 5: take_ownership / release_ownership through existing v1 case-lock plumbing (WebSocket reflects to desktop)
- PR 6: call-senior button via OS dialer intent (`tel:` URL) + on-call schedule lookup
- PR 7: WebAuthn platform-authenticator (biometric) enforcement when `[security] require_hardware_key = true`
- PR 8: documentation + ops runbook (device register, push-path test, device revoke)

## Provisional answers
- Q1: A (Tauri Mobile) — Rust end-to-end; fallback to B (PWA) if Tauri Mobile maturity blocks shipping; decide on prototype evidence
- Q2: both — APNs+FCM direct for Bluesky profile; ntfy.sh-compatible for labeler profile (config switch)
- Q3: A (platform authenticator only) — external YubiKey on mobile is unrealistic for P1 response
- Q4: A (Polaris-internal `oncall_schedule` table) — labelers don't want a PagerDuty dep just for rotation
- Q5: mobile writes go through v1 case-lock infra; WebSocket already broadcasts (no mobile-specific shortcut)

## Rust-quality notes
- **No mobile-specific endpoints (REQ-8).** If mobile needs an endpoint the desktop doesn't, add it to both. Symmetric API surface; one place to test.
- **Push payload has NO PII (REQ-8 / AC-8).** Payload shape: `{ "type": "p1", "incident_id": "..." }`. No moderator name, no subject content. Unit-test asserts no PII fields in the serialized payload.
- **`tonic` is not the right tool for APNs/FCM** — those are HTTP/2 (APNs) and HTTPS/JSON (FCM). Use `a2` (Apple Push) and `fcm` (Firebase) crates, or roll thin clients via `reqwest` with workspace pinning.
- **Per-device token rotation** is a `tokio::sync::Mutex<HashMap<…>>` over the device-token store. Per rust-quality §10, do NOT hold the guard across `.await` — clone-and-release.
- The notifications worker is a `tokio::task::JoinSet` over per-device tasks (rust-quality §10) so a single bad push token doesn't poison the queue.

## External references
- Tauri Mobile: https://v2.tauri.app/start/prerequisites/#mobile-targets
- APNs HTTP/2 spec: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/usernotifications/setting_up_a_remote_notification_server/sending_notification_requests_to_apns
- FCM HTTP v1: https://firebase.google.com/docs/cloud-messaging/migrate-v1
- WebAuthn platform authenticator: https://www.w3.org/TR/webauthn-2/
- iOS ASWebAuthenticationSession: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/authenticationservices/aswebauthenticationsession
- Android Custom Tabs: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/android/custom-tabs/

## Blocks / blocked-by
- Independent of #99, #105, ML/Ozone/Trust epics.
- Soft-related to TPM/HW-token signing epics (mobile baseline is platform-authenticator only; external HW keys are a future issue).
